content: ESA - The mission Science & Exploration The mission 29697 views 56 likes ESA / Science & Exploration / Space Science / Mars Express Mars Express set off on 2 June 2003. At this time of year the positions of Earth and Mars made for the shortest possible route, a condition that occurs once every 26 months. The intrepid spacecraft began its six-month journey from the Baikonur launch site in Kazakhstan on board a Russian Soyuz/Fregat launcher. Having escaped Earth's pull, Mars Express was sent on course for the Red Planet, cruising at a velocity of 10 800 kilometres an hour, relative to Earth. Six days before arrival on 25 December 2003, Mars Express ejected the Beagle 2 lander which was to have made its own way to the correct landing site on the surface.
